title: Clinical Review Desk Standard: Deciding Utilization Management Program Cases
content:
This standard of the Utilization Management Program clinical review desk governs when and how a coverage review case is decided.

**1. Timeframes.** A standard case is decided within the package's standard decision hours and an urgent case within its urgent decision hours, each counted from the receipt of the case.

**2. Missing information.** When the clinical information needed to apply the criteria is missing, the reviewer makes the package's number of outreach attempts to the prescriber and the case pends; it is decided as soon as the information is received.

**3. Waiting period before a missing-information denial.** A case with an information request outstanding may be denied for missing information only after the package's information wait days (calendar days) have fully elapsed since the information request, counting the request date as day zero.

**4. Outcomes.** A case is approved with the reason *criteria met* when the clinical information on file meets the package's criteria for the drug and review type, and denied with *criteria not met*, *step not satisfied* or *missing clinical information* otherwise. A request for a drug that already has an approval of the same type in force is denied with *already approved* unless it is a renewal inside the renewal window.

**5. One decision per case.** While the package provides that a case takes exactly one decision, a case may be decided only when it has no approval, denial or withdrawal yet.

**6. Reviewer level.** Approvals may be made by a reviewer at the package's lowest approving level (a pharmacist) or above; an urgent denial needs a physician reviewer when the package requires a physician for urgent denials.

## The waiting period worked through

The clock starts on the date of the information request recorded on the case (day zero); the comparison is with the date of the intended denial, and the denial must fall after the last waiting day — the last waiting day itself does not qualify.

| Package wait | Information request dated (day zero) | Last waiting day | Earliest date a missing-information denial is allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 days | 3 June | 10 June (day 7) | 11 June |
| 5 days | 3 June | 8 June (day 5) | 9 June |
| 3 days | 3 June | 6 June (day 3) | 7 June |

*Hypothetical dates.* On 10 June, under a 7-day wait, the period has not yet fully elapsed and the case may not be denied for missing information; on 11 June it may. The waiting period does not hold back a decision once the information arrives: the case is then decided on it.

## Decision eligibility at a glance

| Case history | May the case be decided now |
|---|---|
| Opened, nothing after it | Yes |
| Already approved, denied or withdrawn | No |
